core_obligations: Fix notation and reduce to a normal local domain (proof lines 3840-3864): the ring of global sections of the alteration is a finite module over the ring, and it is a normal domain because the alteration is regular, hence normal; this shows the integral closure is finite and reduces the third assertion to the normality of the adic completion of the ring of global sections; decomposing that completion as a product of the completions at the finitely many maximal ideals reduces further to the case where the ring of global sections equals the base ring.

Normality of the completion (proof lines 3866-3880): after the base change to the adic completion the alteration stays regular, its ring of global sections is the completion, and it is connected because that completion is local; a connected normal Noetherian scheme is integral, so its global sections form a normal domain, which is the normality of the completion that was required.

Regularity of the generic formal fibre (proof lines 3882-3894): the base change to the generic point of the base is finite and faithfully flat over the generic point, the base change of the alteration to the completion is regular, hence so is its restriction over the generic point viewed as a limit of opens, and regularity descends along the resulting finite faithfully flat map onto the generic formal fibre.
proof_roadmap: Use the ring of global sections of the alteration to see that the integral closure is finite and to reduce the normality statement to the completion.
Reduce to the case where the global sections equal the base ring, then use connectedness and normality to conclude that the completion is a normal domain.
Read the regularity of the generic formal fibre off from the regularity of the completion base change and descent along a finite faithfully flat map.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a local Noetherian domain admitting a regular alteration, the ring becomes regular after inverting some nonzero element, the integral closure is finite, the adic completion of that integral closure is normal, and the generic formal fibre is regular (statement lines 3826-3838). The proof (proof lines 3840-3898) uses the ring of global sections of the alteration to obtain finiteness and normality statements, reduces the third assertion to a normality statement for a completion, and deduces the fourth by descent of regularity along a finite faithfully flat map. H3: three related assertions with several reductions, written out in full.
